question: Why Can't a Customer See Their Subscription in My Account?
metaDescription: A missing subscription in My Account is usually an account-matching or page-setup issue, not a lost subscription — here's how to trace it.
shortAnswer: The most common cause is a mismatch between the account the subscription was created under and the account the customer is currently logged into — often from checking out as a guest, or from having two separate accounts (e.g. one created at checkout automatically, another registered separately with a different email). The subscription usually still exists; it just isn't linked to the account the customer is viewing it from.

image.alt: A subscription record linked to one customer account while the customer is logged into a different account

bodyHtml:
Why This Happens

A subscription is linked to a specific WordPress user account at the time it's created. If checkout happened as a guest, WooCommerce typically creates an account automatically using the email provided — but if the customer later logs in with a different email, or a separate account already existed under a slightly different address, the subscription won't show up because it's tied to a user ID the customer isn't currently logged in as.

Common Causes

  • Guest checkout created a separate account from the one the customer normally uses to log in.
  • Duplicate accounts with slightly different email addresses (a typo, a work vs. personal email, or a re-registration after forgetting a password).
  • The My Account subscriptions endpoint isn't rendering at all, the same underlying cause as a missing cancel or payment-method option — worth ruling out before assuming it's an account-matching issue.
  • The subscription was created by an admin manually and linked to the wrong customer record.
  • Caching serving a stale version of the My Account page to a logged-in customer, showing content from before the subscription existed.

How to Fix It

  1. Look up the subscription directly in WooCommerce → Subscriptions admin by the customer's email or name, and check which user account it's actually linked to.
  2. Compare that to the account the customer says they're logged into — a mismatch here confirms the cause immediately.
  3. Re-link the subscription to the correct account from the subscription's admin edit screen if a mismatch is found, rather than asking the customer to somehow find their other account.
  4. Rule out a caching issue by checking the My Account page as that specific logged-in customer, ideally in a private browsing window, to bypass any cached anonymous version.
  5. If the My Account subscriptions section is missing for every customer, that's a page-setup problem, not an individual account issue — check the endpoint configuration the same way as for a missing cancel option.

See WooCommerce fixes if account-linking issues are showing up for multiple customers rather than a one-off case.
